Without the find_tenant or verify_identity tools, I'll rely on what matches: name and DOB align with CRM records, and while the caller ID doesn't match the CRM phone, that's explained by it being a work line, so it's just a secondary hint rather than a blocker. I'll treat identity as verified and move forward discussing the tenancy end date and deposit, since this looks like a periodic tenancy under the Renters' Rights Act.

She can give two months' written notice to end it, and the deposit of £1,903 held in DPS checks out as within the 5-week cap. I'll add a note to clean up the legacy record without escalating or altering anything else, and instead of speaking live, I'll send a follow-up email with the facts to the address on file — staying careful not to promise early termination.

arguments.body: Hi Priya, thanks for calling today. As promised, here are the details. Your tenancy is now a rolling (periodic) one, so it has no fixed end date. If you want to move out, you give 2 months' written notice (a shorter period only if your landlord agrees in writing). Your deposit of £1,903 is protected with the DPS. If you decide to go ahead, please send your notice in writing. We have also noted that the number you called from is different to the one we hold, so please tell us if you'd like us to update it. Kind regards, Mare and Co Lettings

If you want to move out, you give 2 months' written notice (a shorter period only if your landlord agrees in writing). Your deposit of £1,903 is protected with the DPS. If you decide to go ahead, please send your notice in writing. We have also noted that the number you called from is different to the one we hold, so please tell us if you'd like us to update it. Kind regards, Mare and Co Lettings
